answer: An economy paying agents to inspect a bridge or a dune beacon could admit one earning key per certified secure chip. Validators challenge the chip to sign fresh nonces, check its manufacturer certificate, and reject a certificate already assigned to another key. A nonexportable secret prevents cloning one device into a farm. Every extra alias needs another genuine chip, adding purchase and operating costs even in parallel. This assumes honest certification and extraction resistance; hardware farms can still buy entry, and newcomers need compatible devices.
